title: portableapps: preserve plugins directory across upgrades
description:
## What this does

Adds a `[SpecialPaths]` `Plugins=` entry to `packaging/portableapps/appinfo.tmpl`, telling the PortableApps.com installer to preserve the global plugins directory (and its per-version subfolders) across upgrades instead of deleting it.

## Why

Per the PortableApps.com Format spec, `Plugins=` marks a directory as excluded from the installer's default "wipe and replace" upgrade behavior. Wireshark's template never set this, so every major-version upgrade of Wireshark Portable silently deletes the previous version's global plugins folder — including any custom/manually-added plugins, with no warning and no way to recover them.

## Status

This is a small, low-risk config change, but **I have not yet tested it against an actual PortableApps.com build/upgrade cycle** (no Windows/NSIS environment available to me right now). Opening as a draft to get early feedback on the approach before investing in a full test. Happy to test the upgrade scenario (old version + custom plugin + upgrade) if a maintainer confirms this is the right direction.

Fixes #15550

notes.body:
Closing to resubmit from a cleaner branch this branch picked up an already merged commit from an earlier MR (!23609) along with the intended change. Reopening from a branch based on current master with just the `appinfo.tmpl` change.

###

changes_data.diff:
@@ -26,3 +26,9 @@ DisplayVersion=@PROJECT_VERSION@
 [Control]
 Icons=1
 Start=@PORTABLEAPPS_NAME@.exe
+
+[SpecialPaths]
+# Preserve the global plugins directory (and its per-version subfolders,
+# e.g. plugins\4.4\epan) across upgrades instead of deleting it.
+# See gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/issues/15550
+Plugins=App\Wireshark\plugins

commits_data.title: portable: Disable automatic updates for PortableApps
commits_data.message:
portable: Disable automatic updates for PortableApps

Detect PortableApps installations by checking for the AppInfo directory
alongside the App folder using get_progfile_dir(). This prevents
portable versions from attempting to use the standard update mechanisms
(WinSparkle/Sparkle).

- Runtime detection (not compile-time #ifdef PORTABLE)
- Directory layout check (not environment variable)
- Minimal changes with detailed comments

Fixes #20867
